items.title: Six Attentions of Calm-and-Insight Practice, and What Each Accomplishes

items.zh: 勝解思擇作意者，謂由此故，或有最初思擇諸法，或奢摩他而為上首。寂靜作意者，謂由此故，或有最初安心於內、或毘鉢舍那而為上首。一分修作意者，謂由此故，於奢摩他毘鉢舍那、隨修一分。具分修作意者，謂由此故，二分雙修。無間作意者，謂一切時無間無斷相續而轉。殷重作意者，謂不慢緩加行方便。
items.en: The attention of resolute discernment is that by which one either, at the outset, discerns phenomena, or does so with calm as its head. The attention of stilling is that by which one either, at the outset, settles the mind within, or does so with insight as its head. The attention of partial cultivation is that by which one cultivates only one of calm and insight; the attention of full cultivation is that by which one cultivates both together. The uninterrupted attention is that which at all times proceeds continuously, without gap or break. The earnest attention is applying oneself to the means without slackness.

items.zh: 此中由勝解思擇作意故、淨修智見。由寂靜作意故，生長輕安。由一分、具分修作意故，於諸蓋中心得解脫。由無間、殷重作意故，於諸結中心得解脫。又由無間作意故、終不徒然而捨身命。由殷重作意故，速證通慧。
items.en: Herein, through the attention of resolute discernment one purifies knowledge-and-vision; through the attention of stilling one grows pliancy; through partial and full cultivation the mind is freed from the [five] hindrances; through uninterrupted and earnest attention the mind is freed from the fetters. Moreover, through uninterrupted attention one never lays down body and life in vain; and through earnest attention one swiftly realises the higher knowledge.

items.title: Conforming and Counteracting: Wearying of the Aggregates, Then Casting Affliction Off

items.zh: 隨順作意者，謂由此故，厭壞所緣，順斷煩惱。對治作意者，謂由此故，正捨諸惑，任持於斷，令諸煩惱遠離相續。
items.en: The conforming attention is that by which one wearies of and breaks down the object, thereby conforming to the severance of affliction. The counteracting attention is that by which one actually casts off the afflictions, holds firm to their severance, and makes the afflictions withdraw from the [mind-]continuum.

items.title: Two Attentions of Encouragement: The Six Recollections, and Checking One's Own Progress

items.zh: 順清淨作意者，謂由此故，修六隨念，或復思惟隨一妙事。順觀察作意者，謂由此故，觀諸煩惱斷與未斷；或復觀察自己所證，及先所觀諸法道理。
items.en: The attention conducing to purity is that by which one cultivates the six recollections, or contemplates some single excellent thing. The attention conducing to investigation is that by which one observes whether the afflictions are severed or not, or examines what one has oneself realised and whether one's prior contemplation of phenomena accords with the principle.

items.title: How Attention "Runs": From Forced Effort to Spontaneous Flow at Four Decisive Times

items.zh: 力勵運轉作意者，謂修始業未得作意者所有作意。有間運轉作意者，謂已得作意，於上慢緩修加行者所有作意。有功用運轉作意者，謂即於此勇猛精進無有慢緩修加行者所有作意。
items.en: The attention that runs by forced effort is the attention of a beginner who has not yet attained [threshold] attention. The attention that runs with interruption is the attention of one who has attained [threshold] attention but cultivates the higher levels' application slackly. The attention that runs with effort is the attention of one who cultivates that same application with vigorous energy and no slackness.

items.zh: 自然運轉作意者，謂於四時決定作意。一、得作意時；二、正入、已入根本定時；三、修現觀時；四、正得、已得阿羅漢時。
items.en: The attention that runs spontaneously is the settled attention at four times: first, when [threshold] attention is attained; second, when entering or having entered a root dhyāna; third, when cultivating direct realisation; fourth, when attaining or having attained arhatship.

items.title: Insight and Calm Again, and the Two Attentions of Purification

items.zh: 思擇作意者，謂毘鉢舍那品作意。內攝作意者，謂奢摩他品作意。淨障作意者，謂由此故，棄捨諸漏，永害麁重。依止成辦所行清淨作意者，謂由此故，依離一切麁重之身，雖行一切所緣境界，而諸煩惱不復現行。
items.en: The attention of discernment is the insight-type attention. The attention of inward gathering is the calm-type attention. The attention that purifies the obstruction is that by which one casts off the outflows and forever destroys the coarse unfitness. The attention of the purity of conduct accomplished in reliance is that by which, relying on a body freed of all coarse unfitness, one moves through every object yet no affliction manifests again.

items.title: The Last Four Attentions: The Three Vehicles' Distinct Ways of Turning the Mind

items.zh: 他所建立作意者，謂諸聲聞所有作意。要從他音，乃能於內如理作意故。內增上取作意者，謂諸獨覺及諸菩薩所有作意。以不從師而覺悟故。
items.en: The attention established by others is the attention of the śrāvakas, for they can rouse sound inner attention only from another's voice. The attention grasped by inner ascendancy is the attention of the pratyekabuddhas and the bodhisattvas, for they awaken without following a teacher.

items.zh: 廣大作意者，謂諸菩薩為善了知生死過失、出離方便，發弘誓願趣大菩提所有作意。遍行作意者，謂佛世尊現見一切無障礙智相應作意。若諸菩薩遍於三乘及五明處方便善巧所有作意。
items.en: The vast attention is the attention of bodhisattvas who, in order to know well the faults of saṃsāra and the means of release, arouse the great vow and head towards great awakening. The all-pervading attention is the attention associated with the World-Honoured Buddha's unobstructed knowledge that directly sees all things; and also the attention of bodhisattvas skilled in means across the three vehicles and the five sciences.

items.title: Correlating the Seven Root Attentions with the Forty (Part 1)

items.zh: 此中了相作意攝緣法、緣義；餘六作意唯攝緣義。緣身等境四種作意，遍在七攝。了相、勝解、加行究竟果作意通攝勝解、真實作意；觀察作意唯攝勝解；餘三作意唯攝真實。此就前門。就餘門者，當知隨應。
items.en: Here the knowing-marks attention subsumes both attention-on-the-letter and attention-on-the-meaning; the other six attentions subsume only attention-on-the-meaning. The four attentions on body, feeling, mind, and phenomena are present across all seven. The knowing-marks, resolute-conviction, and fruit-of-consummation attentions subsume both the resolute-conviction and the real attention; the investigation attention subsumes only resolute-conviction; the remaining three subsume only the real. This is by the former approach; by the other approach, know it applies as fitting.

items.zh: 七種作意皆攝有學及非學非無學二種作意。亦攝無學作意。謂清淨地了相作意及加行究竟果作意。了相、勝解、觀察作意，攝遍知作意。餘三作意，攝正斷作意。加行究竟果作意，攝已斷作意。
items.en: All seven attentions subsume both the trainee's and the neither-trainee-nor-adept's attention; they also subsume the adept's — namely the pure-stage knowing-marks attention and the fruit-of-consummation attention. The knowing-marks, resolute-conviction, and investigation attentions subsume the full-knowledge attention; the remaining three subsume the active-severance attention; the fruit-of-consummation attention subsumes the already-severed attention.

items.zh: 觀察作意，唯攝有分別影像所緣作意。餘六作意通攝二種。事邊際所緣作意遍一切攝。所作成辦所緣作意，若就初門，遍一切攝。就第二門，唯加行究竟果作意所攝。最初勝解思擇作意皆所不攝。若奢摩他而為上首，遍一切攝。若最初寂靜，若毘鉢舍那而為上首，當知亦爾。
items.en: The investigation attention subsumes only the discriminated-image-object attention; the other six subsume both kinds. The limit-of-the-thing-object attention is subsumed across all. The task-accomplished-object attention, by the first approach, is subsumed across all; by the second approach, only the fruit-of-consummation attention subsumes it. The initial resolute-discernment attention is subsumed by none of the seven; but with calm as its head it is subsumed across all — and likewise the initial stilling, and with insight as its head.

items.zh: 前六作意，通攝一分及具分修。加行究竟果作意，唯攝具分修。無間作意、殷重作意遍一切攝。隨順作意，初二所攝。對治作意，遠離、加行究竟二作意攝，及攝樂作意一分所攝。順清淨作意，唯攝樂一分所攝。順觀察斷未斷作意，唯觀察作意所攝。此就斷對治說。若就所餘，隨應當知。
items.en: The first six attentions subsume both partial and full cultivation; the fruit-of-consummation attention subsumes only full cultivation. The uninterrupted and earnest attentions are subsumed across all. The conforming attention is subsumed by the first two; the counteracting attention by seclusion and consummation-of-means, and by a part of delight-in-gathering. The purity-conducing attention is subsumed by a part of delight-in-gathering; the investigation-of-whether-severed attention is subsumed only by the investigation attention — this by the severance-counteracting approach; by the other, know it applies as fitting.

items.zh: 力勵運轉作意皆所不攝。有間、有功用運轉作意，乃至攝樂作意所攝。
items.en: It is not included in the attention that proceeds by forceful effort. It is included in the attention that proceeds with interruption and with effort, and so on through the attention that gathers joy.

blocks.text: Today continues the forty attentions. Two passages stand out for practice: how attention moves from forced effort to spontaneous flow, and how the three vehicles turn the mind differently. Read the first with your own practice in mind; most meditators recognise the stages.

Six attentions belong to calm-and-insight practice, each with its own work. Then **conforming** attention, which wearies of the aggregates, and **counteracting** attention, which casts off afflictions. Master Cháng Bǎi maps the counteracting functions onto the stages of each act of cutting (Day 19): the severing antidote is the uninterrupted path; the holding antidote, the path of liberation; the distancing antidote, the path of further progress.

The attentions of **full knowledge**, **active severance**, and **already-severed** mark the same sequence: one first knows the object without yet cutting the affliction; then knows and cuts at once; then everything afterwards is attention of one who has cut.
Two attentions encourage: the **six recollections** (of the Buddha, Dharma, Saṅgha, discipline, generosity, and the gods), which lift a discouraged mind; and checking one's own progress.

items: **by forced effort** (力勵運轉): Master Cháng Bǎi: "a practitioner just beginning calm and insight, not yet at threshold concentration, must push hard";

**with interruption** (有間缺): after some attainment, practice is slack. Venerable Miào Jìng adds a subtler sense: in threshold concentration one still applies thoughts of renunciation and non-harm, so the samādhi is interspersed with observation;
**spontaneously** (自然運轉): at four decisive times: on attaining threshold attention, entering a root dhyāna, cultivating direct realisation, and attaining arhatship.

blocks.text: The lesson is reassuring: effort is the normal beginning. Spontaneity comes later, as the fruit of the effort, not as a substitute for it.

Two attentions purify: one of the object, one of the mind. The last four attentions mark the vehicles. Attention "**established by others**" belongs to śrāvakas, who arouse sound attention only from another's voice; attention "**grasped by inner ascendancy**" belongs to pratyekabuddhas and bodhisattvas, who awaken without a teacher in their final life. The **vast attention** (廣大作意) is the bodhisattva's.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the vast attention "is making the great bodhi vow; it has nothing to do with cultivating concentration", which is why it does not belong among the seven root attentions. The bodhisattva path is defined by a vow, not by a meditative state.

The treatise then maps the seven root attentions of Day 82 onto the forty: each root attention contains several of the forty. The two lists are two views of the same practice: the seven as a sequence of stages, the forty as a catalogue of functions.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the attentions of full knowledge, active severance, and already-severed?
options: full knowledge knows the object without yet cutting affliction; active severance does both; already-severed is all attention after affliction is cut
quiz.why: The attention of full knowledge knows the object but does not yet sever affliction; active severance "does both things at once"; already-severed "is all the attention that occurs after affliction has been severed." Master Cháng Bǎi: full knowledge belongs to the preparatory path. Venerable Miào Jìng: already-severed is subsequent wisdom.

quiz.q: Counteracting attention casts off afflictions, holds their severance, and distances them. Which three antidotes and paths, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: severing antidote — uninterrupted path; holding antidote — liberation path; distancing antidote — path of progress
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The severing antidote belongs to the uninterrupted path, actually cutting; the holding antidote to the liberation path, already cut and liberated"; "the distancing antidote to the path of progress, gradually moving away." Venerable Miào Jìng maps them likewise.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, at which four times is attention "spontaneous"?
options: attaining threshold attention, entering a root dhyāna, cultivating direct realisation, attaining arhatship
quiz.why: "The attention that runs spontaneously is the settled attention at four times: first, when … attention is attained; second, when entering or having entered a root dhyāna; third, when cultivating direct realisation; fourth, when attaining or having attained arhatship." Venerable Miào Jìng: long recitation becomes effortless, yet is still attention.

quiz.q: Whose is the "attention that runs by forced effort," per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: a beginner in calm and insight who hasn't yet reached threshold concentration and must push hard
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "A practitioner just beginning calm and insight, not yet at threshold concentration, must encourage themselves with great effort." Venerable Miào Jìng: not yet concentrated, so none of the seven root attentions includes it.

quiz.q: Attention "with interruption" belongs to one who has attained attention but practices slackly. Why the interruption, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: in threshold concentration one still applies thoughts of renunciation, non-anger, non-harm — the samādhi is interspersed with thought
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "In threshold concentration one practices thoughts of renunciation, non-anger, non-harm — these observations." When there's no gap, one has the form-realm dhyāna. The reading note's "looking up the teaching" differs.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, whose are the attention "established by others" and that "grasped by inner ascendancy"?
options: the first is śrāvakas, who need another's voice; the second pratyekabuddhas and bodhisattvas, who awaken without a teacher
quiz.why: "The attention established by others is the attention of the śrāvakas, for they can rouse sound inner attention only from another's voice. The attention grasped by inner ascendancy is … of the pratyekabuddhas and the bodhisattvas, for they awaken without following a teacher."

quiz.q: The text says the vast attention is subsumed by none of the seven. Why, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the vast attention is arousing the great bodhi vow, unrelated to meditative concentration, so it isn't one of the seven
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The vast attention is making the vow — the great bodhi vow; it has nothing to do with cultivating concentration, so it isn't among the seven." Venerable Miào Jìng, citing Kuiji: bodhisattvas' vast practice differs from the seven, which serve one's own benefit.
